findings.topic: Branched cover and uniform peripheral map
findings.assessment: Character zero on both the circle meridian and its longitude, using linking number two, makes its boundary split into two degree-one torus covers. Branch filling along the primitive lift of the squared knot meridian produces the actual branched-cover exterior. The two downstairs classes mu and mu+lambda form an integral basis. Their claimed signed lifts (-1,2) and (-1,1), expressed in the same raw triangulation with orientations inherited rather than independently chosen, give lambda=(0,-1) by subtraction. The resulting matrix has determinant one. Linearity therefore proves the map for every integer parameter; this is not an extrapolation from sample fillings. In particular (1,-3n) lifts to (-1,2+3n) on each circle cusp.

findings.topic: Branched annulus framing and relative pants filling
findings.assessment: The double branched cover of the twice-punctured disk is an annulus. A disk-neighborhood ball with two trivial branch arcs lifts to A times I, a solid torus; its two lifted boundary circles are parallel cores. The annulus pushoff is locally the lift of the disk longitude, so it supplies the required framing with no extra integer term. Opposite orientations of the lifted cores reverse both meridian and longitude, preserving the unoriented parameter. Removing the cores gives Q times S1 with s0=s1+s2. Filling s_j+t_j f extends the product Seifert structure without exceptional fibers and leaves a solid torus with primitive outer meridian s0+(t1+t2)f. This proves the relative homeomorphism because a solid torus is determined relative to its boundary by its primitive meridian, not merely by its first homology.
